failed_checks.title: RFC 3339 leap-second restrictions are not enforced
failed_checks.expected: A second value of 60 is accepted only at a real leap-second instant, with non-Z local time shifted by its numeric offset; impossible positions are rejected.
failed_checks.actual: The regex accepts :60 at every otherwise well-formed date, time, and offset. 2030-01-01T12:34:60Z, 1990-12-31T12:00:60Z, and 1990-12-31T23:59:60-08:00 all validate successfully.
failed_checks.reproduction: Run the independent date-time controls recorded in verification-evidence/independent-probes.json. Each named invalid leap-second case has actual=false for rejection, meaning the schema validator accepted it.
failed_checks.impact: The custom FormatChecker is shared by every format: date-time field, so impossible instants can pass all BATCH-03 schemas despite the claimed RFC 3339 semantic lock.
failed_checks.authority: RFC 3339 sections 5.6-5.8; JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 validation section 7.3.1.

failed_checks.title: IMPLEMENTATION_REPORT.json omits recheck_commands
failed_checks.expected: A non-empty recheck_commands list in the target-commit implementation report, usable as the verifier's explicit rerun input.
failed_checks.actual: The field is absent. The verifier independently used the current plan acceptance_commands and the explicit dispatcher commands, rather than inventing an implementation-report field.

regression_risks: Because one global custom FormatChecker serves every format: date-time schema field, F-B03-V3-001 is broader than the shipment probe used to reproduce it.
